notes:
TickOracleHook keeps an on-chain time-weighted tick oracle for every pool it is installed on, modelled on Uniswap v3's Oracle library, and does nothing else.

Repository: src/TickOracleHook.sol (the hook), src/TickOracleToken.sol (the ERC-20 this launch mints), src/base/BaseHook.sol (PoolManager-only callbacks adapted from v4-periphery; its constructor validates the deploying address against getHookPermissions), src/libraries/Oracle.sol (the ring buffer ported from v3), src/interfaces/ITickOracleHook.sol, src/HookFlags.sol, src/HookMiner.sol and script/Deploy.s.sol (the Sepolia launch). Foundry, solc 0.8.26; forge-std, v4-core, solmate and openzeppelin-contracts vendored under lib/ as ordinary files. Tests place the hook by CREATE2 at an address carrying exactly its flags against a real PoolManager, drive swaps through several pools across warped blocks, and check observe and consult against independently computed values.

Permissions: afterInitialize and afterSwap, and only those two. getHookPermissions returns those two fields true and the other twelve false, so the mined address carries exactly 0x1040 (AFTER_INITIALIZE_FLAG 1 << 12, AFTER_SWAP_FLAG 1 << 6). beforeSwap is off; both swap returnDelta flags are off; every liquidity and donate flag is off.

Behaviour: per pool, a ring buffer of observations, each a uint32 block timestamp (wrapping) and an int56 tick cumulative, with an index, a cardinality and a cardinalityNext. _afterInitialize writes observation 0 with a zero cumulative and records the initial tick. _afterSwap writes a new observation only when the block timestamp has advanced past the newest one, accumulating the previously recorded tick over the elapsed seconds, then records the post-swap tick: at most one observation per pool per block, and a swap's own price impact counts only from the next block, as v3 does. _afterSwap returns (afterSwap.selector, 0) on every path, so a swap settles exactly as it would with no hook attached. Both callbacks override BaseHook's internal virtuals, so the onlyPoolManager check on every external callback stands.

Reads and growth, callable by anyone: increaseObservationCardinalityNext(PoolKey, uint16) grows a pool's buffer from an initial cardinality of 1 up to a hard cap of 1024, reverting with CardinalityTooLarge past it. observe(PoolKey, uint32[]) returns int56 tick cumulatives, interpolating between the two surrounding observations found by binary search, extrapolating from the newest when secondsAgo is 0, and reverting with TargetPredatesOldestObservation when a requested time precedes the oldest observation. consult(PoolKey, uint32) returns the arithmetic-mean tick over the window as int24, rounded toward negative infinity, and reverts with ZeroWindow on a zero window. Timestamp comparisons follow v3's Oracle.lte across uint32 wraparound. A pool the hook never initialized reverts with OracleCardinalityCannotBeZero.

What the hook deliberately does not have: no owner, admin, role or privileged address; no currency handling of any kind, it never takes, settles, mints or holds a token or ETH and has no receive or fallback; no fee; no pause, proxy, delegatecall, selfdestruct, or setter beyond cardinality growth.

Constructor: constructor(IPoolManager) and nothing more. The single argument is the Uniswap v4 PoolManager on Ethereum Sepolia.

Token: TickOracleToken, name "Tick Oracle Signal", symbol TOS, 18 decimals, a plain OpenZeppelin ERC20 whose entire fixed supply is minted once, in the constructor, to msg.sender, with no mint or burn entry point afterwards, no owner, and no functions beyond the standard.

Pool: TOS paired with USDC on Sepolia (0x1c7d4b196cb0c7b01d743fbc6116a902379c7238) at fee tier 3000, whose canonical tick spacing is 60, initialized on the hook at initialPrice 79228162514264337593543950336 = 2**96, the sqrtPriceX96 of 1:1, which reads the same whichever side of the pair the token sorts to.
